about: Load-bearing prose claims of this package, each bound to a machine-checkable fact about the artifact. Run: python3 scripts/verify_claims.py. The failure mode this exists to catch is ASSERTED + UNBACKED — the docs say it, the artifact does not do it. See scripts/verify_claims.py for why the existing phrase-linter cannot express these checks.

claims.claim: The prediction register is cryptographically (GPG) signed; predictions are signed before their data are released.

detect.exclude_note: Meta-documentation about this very checker necessarily quotes the false claim it detects (e.g. when describing the negative control). Excluded for the same reason CHANGELOG.md is excluded from count claims: it is a record *about* claims, not an assertion. Noted honestly rather than silently hedged — the tool flagged its own documentation on first run.
detect.unless_note: Hedges fall into three families: (a) explicit self-correction (overstat/was false/v12.3), (b) explicit non-execution (not yet/never/unexecuted/not GPG-signed), (c) normative or definitional statements of the protocol rather than assertions about this register ('must be', 'or equivalent', 'is one whose'). Family (c) is the subtle one: a protocol spec may legitimately describe signing it does not perform. Validated empirically: these hedges still fire on the historical v12.2 wording (see docs/claim_verification.md).

claims.note: THE historical failure. At v12.2 this claim was asserted in the deposited JOSS paper while all ten register entries were unsigned scaffolds. This check is the automated form of the `grep SCAFFOLD` that finally caught it.

claims.claim: The register contains N pre-registered predictions (N stated in prose must match the register).
claims.note: Catches count drift as the register grows. The 8 -> 10 drift (v12.1/v12.2 added P9, P10) survived in fourteen places until the July 2026 audit found it by hand.

claims.claim: The publication strategy comprises N papers (N stated in prose must match papers/ on disk).
claims.note: Paper E was added after the 'four-paper strategy' phrasing was written. CHANGELOG.md is excluded by design: it is a historical record, and per project policy history is annotated rather than rewritten — a v12.0 entry describing the then-current four-paper strategy is accurate as history.

claims.claim: N scoring pipelines are active (N stated in prose must match scripts/predictions_score_P*.py).
Each scorecard records the SHA-256 of the pipeline output it scored, so the evidence chain is verifiable.
claims.note: Exact, mechanical: recomputes each hash. Catches a scorecard drifting from the output it claims to describe.

claims.claim: Every major artifact is schema-validated; each pipeline output names its schema.
No surviving claim that GSC explains a real observational anomaly (all such claims were retracted).

verify.pattern: GSC explains (?:a |the )?(?:real |unsolved |experimental )*anomaly|explains the (?:neutron|beam-trap) anomaly|first explained anomaly

claims.note: The v12.0 release claimed the neutron-lifetime anomaly was explained; v12.1 retracted it. This keeps the retraction enforced.

claims.claim: Citation metadata points at the canonical public repository.
claims.note: Guards against citing a private repo (a 404 for anyone following the citation), which was true until July 2026.

claims.claim: The framework document has a section for every prediction in the register.
claims.note: Heuristic-but-useful: the highest PN section number should equal the register size. GSC_Framework.md had no P9/P10 sections at all until the July 2026 audit.

claims.claim: CI asserts the register's prediction count without hardcoding it, so the assertion cannot drift as predictions are added.
claims.note: Added after a real regression: the public repository had fixed a hardcoded `assert len(d) == 8` to 10 (its commit 0296485), and a later package overlay from the working repository silently clobbered that fix with the stale in-package copy — reintroducing a bug the operator had already solved months earlier, and turning CI red. The prose-side count was covered by `prediction-count`; the CI-side count was not. Both workflows now derive the expected number from `predictions_register/P*/prediction.md`, and this claim forbids the hardcoded form from returning. Lesson: a count is a claim wherever it lives, including inside automation.

claims.claim: Prediction pipelines are deterministic: identical inputs produce byte-identical output.
claims.note: Slow (runs all ten pipelines twice). Requires --include-slow.
